I disagree with the principal's decision that every student has to be in at least one extracurricular activity. I think activities are great and I'm in two of them myself, but making them a rule takes away the whole point of them.

The first reason I disagree is that a lot of kids in my school can't stay after school even if they want to. My friend Devin has to take the 3:15 bus because his mom works until 7 and his little sister gets off the elementary bus at 3:40 and somebody has to be home with her. If the principal makes this a rule, what is Devin supposed to do? Either he leaves his sister alone, which is not happening, or he breaks a school rule for something that isn't even his fault. There are also kids who have jobs helping at their family's store, and kids who take care of a grandparent. A rule that a whole group of students physically cannot follow isn't a fair rule. It just punishes the kids who already have the hardest schedules.

Second, forcing somebody to join something usually makes it worse for everyone there, not better. Last year our school made everyone in my grade go to a study club during activity period. Half the people sat there on their phones or put their heads down, and the kids who actually wanted help couldn't get the teacher's attention because she spent the whole time telling people to stop talking. That's what would happen to clubs too. Imagine you're on yearbook and you actually care about it, and then you get six people who were assigned there and don't want to do anything. Now you're doing their pages on top of yours. The clubs that are good are good because the people in them chose to be there.

Some people would say that students who don't join anything are missing out, and honestly that's true sometimes. Clubs and sports are how I met most of my friends, and my coach is probably the adult at school I talk to the most. But you don't fix that by making a rule. You fix it by having more kinds of activities and better times for them. Our school has basketball, football, yearbook, student council, and that's pretty much it. If you're not into sports and you're not into student government, there's nothing. Add a video game club, a cooking club, an art club, something during lunch so the bus kids can do it too. If you did that, more people would sign up on their own and you wouldn't need to force anybody.

So instead of a rule, I think the principal should ask students what they would actually want to join, and then figure out how to make those things happen at a time people can get to. That would get way more kids involved than a rule that some of them can't even follow. Making something required doesn't make people care about it. It usually does the opposite.
